extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, appellate counsel, judges, academics, and law students following Federal Circuit patent law
extracted.subtask_description: A working compilation of the Federal Circuit's precedential patent-law opinions and orders issued in 2024, each annotated with the panel, issues decided, and short practitioner-oriented notes. Useful for tracking doctrinal holdings across patentability, procedure, remedies, jurisdiction, and PTAB practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary injunction; likelihood of success on the merits; irreparable harm; public interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in DexCom v Abbott, Natera v Neogenomics; courts consider parallel district court litigation and IPRs, public interest (e.g., patient access) and weigh irreparable harm; likelihood of success requires careful analysis of claim construction and merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of parallel IPRs on injunctions and merits
rubrics_metrics.description: How parallel district court litigation and IPRs affect injunctions and likelihood-of-success analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. Cir considers whether IPRs undermine district-court claims of likelihood of success (DexCom); cannot ignore ongoing PTAB review when assessing relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract interpretation in patent context
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of earlier settlement and license agreement (including 'No Challenge' covenants and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court enforces express exceptions to No Challenge covenants even when forum selection clauses exist (DexCom); distinguish prior cases when covenant language differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive forum selection clause interaction with enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of exclusive forum selection clauses on enforcement of contractual covenants and IPR activity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forum-selection clauses do not automatically bar IPRs if the parties' agreement expressly excepts certain proceedings from the covenant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction — basic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction issues recurring across opinions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts emphasize construing claims according to intrinsic evidence and avoid importing embodiment aspects as requirements (Promptu v Comcast). Functional constructions may be appropriate where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony on what prior art teaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of expert testimony explaining what a prior-art reference teaches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB and courts may credit one expert over another if expert calculations are grounded in express disclosures of the reference; methodological soundness matters (PacBio v PGTI).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR joinder and participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation of joined party in IPR joinder; consequences when petitioner stops opposing; right of joined party to independently oppose motions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joined party can independently oppose a motion to amend once the original petitioner stops opposing (CyWee v ZTE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend in IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and appellate review of Board denial of motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial may be upheld where appointed experts and facts support PTAB's findings; PTAB must provide reasoned bases for denials (Pfizer v Sanofi motion denial remand noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonobviousness / motivation to combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonobviousness inquiries including motivation to combine and KSR principles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reason for combining references must exist in the record; courts will not accept conclusory motivation or hindsight (Virtek v AssemblyGuidance; PaloAlto v Centripetal). Design-patent nonobviousness should apply Graham factors rather than rigid Rosen/Durling tests (LKQ v GM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a PHOSITA would have had a reasonable expectation of success in combining references or achieving claimed results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certainty is not required; reasonable expectation suffices for obviousness (Salix v Norwich); but outcome depends on art unpredictability and record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective indicia / secondary considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and weighting of objective indicia (commercial success, industry praise, copying, long-felt need, failure of others)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts require appropriate instructions and consideration of different indicia separately; timing and weight vary by indicia (Inline Plastics v Lacerta; LKQ v GM Tweets on secondary considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic industry requirement for ITC §337
rubrics_metrics.description: Showing of domestic industry: economic prong, aggregation versus allocation of expenditures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee must allocate investments among products practicing the asserted patents rather than aggregate across unrelated products (Zircon v ITC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art printed publication (§102) and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed publication analysis under pre-AIA §102(b) and effect of copyright notice on public accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright notice on manuals does not negate public accessibility; distribution to customers can qualify as printed publication (Weber v Provisur).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement and numeric ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Satisfaction of written description for claims reciting numerical ranges
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may find WDR satisfied where the specification discloses overlapping ranges and both endpoints are disclosed; analysis is fact-specific (RAI v Philip Morris).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. §271(e)(1) safe harbor scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of the safe harbor for uses reasonably related to development and submission of information under federal law regulating drugs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safe harbor can shield certain imports or activities reasonably related to regulatory submissions; courts analyze 'solely' language and intent (Edwards Lifesciences v Meril).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and implicit claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether PTAB's implicit claim construction violated the APA and whether parties had notice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may implicitly construe claims when its assessment of a limitation establishes its scope; notice to parties is relevant but not always fatal (Google v EcoFactor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and brief/argument limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on incorporating arguments by reference between briefs to avoid exceeding word counts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation of arguments is not permitted if it would exceed applicable word counts; must comply with FRAP 28 (Promptu order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct / intent and materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for inequitable conduct including but-for materiality, intent to deceive, and collective evaluation of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court evaluates whether withheld or misrepresented references were but-for material and looks at the collective weight of evidence to infer intent; affirmatively egregious misconduct may be per se material (Luv N' Care v Laurain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct evidentiary sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof thresholds for inequitable conduct and consequences on relief
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thin evidence may not suffice; district court findings must be supported by clear and convincing evidence; unclean hands can bar relief (FreshHub v Amazon; Luv N' Care v Laurain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 patent-eligibility (Alice two-step)
rubrics_metrics.description: §101 analysis for abstract ideas and inventive concept under Alice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed to abstract ideas without an inventive concept or technological improvement are ineligible; courts apply familiar indicators of abstractness and analyze whether claims recite well-understood, routine, conventional elements (Chewy v IBM; AI Visualize v Nuance; Beteiro v DraftKings; BroadbandTV v Amazon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Result-effective variable / optimization analysis in obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of molecular weight ranges or other 'result-effective' variables as motivations to optimize
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim recites a result-effective variable, PHOSITA may be motivated to optimize and obviousness may follow even without exact overlapping ranges (Pfizer v Sanofi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim definiteness and apparently contradictory limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: How courts assess claims with multiple limitations that may seem contradictory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts reject indefiniteness where claim limitations can be satisfied together even if drafting could be clearer (Maxell v Amperex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing limitations are not mere 'options'
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations added to overcome prior art that narrow claim scope should be treated as requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added narrowing limitations cannot be treated as optional; they must be given effect (Maxell v Amperex).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of Equivalents evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for particularized linking testimony or expert evidence to prove equivalence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court requires particularized evidence; simple or conclusory testimony may be inadequate; no broad exception for 'easily understandable' cases (NexStep v Comcast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markman and claim construction timing at Rule 12(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a district court may adopt a claim construction in deciding a motion to dismiss without a full Markman hearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No categorical bar to adopting a construction at dismissal stage, but more analysis may be required depending on the record (Utto v MetroTech).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed matter doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether claim limitations concerning communicated content are 'printed matter' lacking patentable weight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If limitations are not claimed for the content they communicate but for functional aspects, they may not be printed matter (IOEngine v Ingenico).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral order doctrine and appellate jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: When interlocutory orders are appealable under the collateral-order doctrine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial of motion to dismiss may not be reviewable absent final judgment; requirements for collateral order review are strict (Copan v Puritan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate review of PTAB factfinding and motivation to combine
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for vacating PTAB findings when motivation to combine is legally insufficient
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts vacate Board findings absent record support for motivation to combine; Board cannot look at references in isolation when combination is at issue (Virtek; Cytiva v JSR remands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic industry aggregation rules (ITC economic prong)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and when patentees may aggregate investments across products to show domestic industry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation is improper when investments are not tied to products practicing the asserted patents; allocation among products or product groups is required (Zircon).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-sale bar and secret process under AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sale of product made by a secret patented process triggers the AIA on-sale bar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale of product more than one year before effective filing date can trigger §102(a) on-sale bar even if process was secret (Celanese v ITC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'publicly disclosed' in §102(b)(2)(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of inventor 'publicly disclosed' communications exception under the AIA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A private (non-secret) offer to sell may not be a 'public disclosure' for §102(b)(2)(B); courts caution against importing prior 'public use' cases into this AIA provision (Sanho v Kaijet).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB rehearing and forfeiture of arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When issues raised in PTAB proceedings are forfeited or preserved on appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional refusal to re-raise arguments in a rehearing request does not necessarily forfeit arguments on appeal; but merits may be dismissed if arguments are conclusory (VoiceTech v UnifiedPatents).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR estoppel and meaning of 'obtaining a claim'
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of estoppel under 35 U.S.C. 316(a)(4) and 37 C.F.R. 42.73(d)(3)(i) regarding amended claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO may lawfully promulgate rules estopping a patentee from obtaining claims in reexaminations that are not patentably distinct from claims cancelled in an adverse IPR, but such estoppel has limits and does not automatically apply to 'issued' claims (SoftView v Apple).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III standing for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Injury-in-fact requirement for appellant standing to appeal adverse PTO or district-court decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative future plans or vague statements about product development are insufficient to establish injury-in-fact (PlatinumOptics v Viavi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory judgment and specific personal jurisdiction via third-party enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: When extra-judicial enforcement activities routed through third parties (e.g., Amazon APEX agreements) constitute purposeful direction for jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APEX takedown agreements that automatically affect sales in a forum can constitute purposeful direction supporting personal jurisdiction (Packet Intelligence v Netscout; SnapPower v LDG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership, assignment ambiguities, and standing to sue
rubrics_metrics.description: How ambiguities in employment agreements and assignment language affect patent ownership and standing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous employment/assignment language can defeat summary judgment on ownership; factual findings required (Core Optical v Nokia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference/priority and §135 time bar (pre-AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority contests and application of the pre-AIA §135 time bar in interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a two-way test to see if pre- and post-critical date claims are materially different; added limitations may be material and trigger time bars (Speck v Bates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Daubert / FRE 702 gatekeeping and damages experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for admissibility of damages expert testimony, e.g., deriving royalties from lump-sum licenses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial courts act as gatekeepers; methodologies tying royalty opinions to facts must be reliable and not merely unilateral recitals of belief (EcoFactor v Google; en banc rehearing granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade secret definition and DTSA enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of trade secret under DTSA and related preliminary injunction/statute of limitations analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts require clear definition of 'trade secret' and analysis of the three-year statute of limitations for DTSA claims; broad labels like 'confidential information' may be insufficient (Insulet v EOFlow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of abstractness for patent eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-settled indicators that claims are abstract (result-focused, functional language, use of generic computer components)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims framed as result-oriented functional language without technological improvement indicate abstractness; courts compare claims to Enfish and other examples (Beteiro v DraftKings; MillerMendel v City of Anna).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skinny-label induced infringement pleading standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Plausibility standard for alleging inducement under Hatch-Waxman context with skinny-labels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleading can be plausible where allegations include skinny label plus promotional statements (Amarin v Hikma); courts resist too-strict pleading standards that would nullify § viii carve-outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction in medical/diagnostic tests — public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Balancing patient access/public interest when preliminary injunctions affect medical test availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may affirm injunctions halting sales when public-interest considerations (patient access) are properly weighed (Natera v Neogenomics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil contempt and fraud/real-party-in-interest issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for contempt and sanctions when parties or real parties-in-interest fail to comply with orders or engage in fraud on the court
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may impose sanctions and fines on record owners or orchestrators for failure to appear and for potential fraud (Backertop v Canary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-Understood, Routine, and Conventional (WUR&C) elements in §101 analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of WUR&C in deciding patent-eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that merely invoke WUR&C computer elements without improving computer technology are ineligible (MillerMendel; Mobile Acuity v Blippar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue preclusion and interlocutory orders merging with final judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: How voluntary dismissals and stipulations can render interlocutory orders final and preclusive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior interlocutory invalidation can become final and preclusive if the plaintiff stipulates to dismissal, potentially mooting related appeals (Koss v Bose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's use of reply briefs and MTA Pilot Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissibility of using reply briefs to supplement written-description support for substitute claims under PTAB pilot programs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB may permit reply briefing to address deficiencies and the MTA Pilot Program aims to let reply briefs correct errors (ZyXel v UNMRI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'patentably distinct' and PTO rulemaking limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of PTO authority to define estoppel concepts and the limits of that authority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO rulemaking under §316(a)(4) can implement estoppel but cannot create new substantive patent law; precise limits await further cases (SoftView v Apple).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article III case-or-controversy for IPR appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appellant lacks a concrete case or controversy to appeal adverse PTAB decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants must show injury-in-fact; absence of any concrete plans or only speculative injuries can defeat appellate standing (PlatinumOptics v Viavi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of attorney fees and §285 exceptional-case analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for awarding attorney fees under §285 and whether fees for parallel IPRs are recoverable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S285 awards generally do not include fees spent on IPRs that defendants voluntarily pursued; district courts must apply appropriate precedent (DragonIP v DishNetwork).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent obviousness framework
rubrics_metrics.description: New framework: apply Graham factors to design patents — analogous art, visual comparison, ordinary designer skill, combining references, and secondary considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the visual impression of the claimed design as a whole and identify a primary reference; require record-supported reason to combine references without hindsight (LKQ v GM en banc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof required for damages based on Entire Market Value Rule (EMVR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of EMVR for royalty/damages awards where patented feature is a small component
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiffs must show the patented feature drove consumer demand and avoid conclusory testimony; EMVR misuse can warrant new trial (Provisur v Weber).

rubrics_metrics.name: §298 evidence of 'advice of counsel' and expert testimony limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on testimony about industry IP-management practices to avoid circumventing §298's intent-of-counsel protections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert testimony cannot substitute third-party non-lawyer advice for advice of counsel; §298 bars using such evidence to negative willfulness (Provisur v Weber).

rubrics_metrics.name: Willfulness and intent evidence for enhanced damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for proving willful infringement and entitlement to enhanced damages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court examines specific evidence of intent; tracking competitor patents or internal charts may be insufficient without more (Provisur v Weber).

rubrics_metrics.name: False advertising via asserting 'patented' product (Lanham Act §43)
rubrics_metrics.description: When falsely claiming a product feature is patented supports a Lanham Act false-advertising claim
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements that a material is patented linked to a product's characteristics can mislead consumers and give rise to §43(a) liability (Crocs v Effervescent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility standard and standard of review for dismissal rulings
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of review for district court determinations whether allegations are factual or conclusory at pleading stage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. Cir holds de novo review is appropriate for certain trial-court determinations about pleadings' factual sufficiency (AlexSam v Aetna).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction — Phillips vs PTAB BRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences between the PTAB’s Broadest Reasonable Construction (BRC) and the Phillips standard used by courts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit recognizes differences; BRC is not binding on courts, and incorporation by reference and provisional claims must be read in light of the specification (DDR Holdings v Priceline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of divided infringement / directing or controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: When an accused infringer is liable for system or method claims involving third-party users
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability requires directing or controlling the acts of third parties such that the accused infringer puts the entire claimed system into use; merchant responsibility for internet access alone may be insufficient (CloudOfChange v NCR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatch-Waxman Orange Book listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for listing patents in FDA Orange Book—must 'claim the drug' for which the NDA was submitted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents that claim only device components but not the drug itself do not meet the listing requirement; listing requires particular pointing out of the drug (Teva v Amneal).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-sale bar under pre-AIA law and hallmarks of commercial offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining whether a quotation or offer constitutes a commercial offer for sale under pre-AIA on-sale bar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts look at the communication as a whole; specificity and completeness can establish an offer rather than an invitation to negotiate, and sending from abroad to a U.S. business can be 'in this country' (Crown Packaging v Belvac).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment requests and judge recusal on remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for reassignment to a new judge after reversal/vacatur on appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fed. Cir may refuse reassignment absent compelling evidence of district judge bias; remand expects objective resolution of disputed issues (Astellas v Sandoz).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate procedure — dismissal after mandate and Director's intervention rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations for granting dismissal after an appeal decision and PTO Director's right to intervene under 35 U.S.C. §143
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts generally disfavor dismissal after issuance of mandate; must consider Director's unconditional right to intervene (Cisco v K. Mizra order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherency and composition/process claim interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: When a property is inherent in a composition or process and its impact on reasonable-expectation-of-success analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a property is inherent in a composition, no reasonable-expectation-of-success showing is necessary to prove obviousness of that property (Cytiva v JSR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of demonstrative evidence and expert screenshots
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility and authentication requirements for screenshots or other electronic demonstratives relied on by experts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthenticated screenshots may be excluded; admissibility requires foundation and reliability (Mirror Worlds v Meta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for bad-faith repeated filings and inherent-power sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of district court inherent powers to sanction repeated meritless filings and bad-faith litigation conduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may impose sanctions under their inherent power in addition to attorney-fees awards for exceptional cases; availability of Rule 11 depends on procedural posture (PS Products v Panther).
